laws.rule: Drivers may not use a portable electronic device while driving, and holding one in the hand counts as use (23 V.S.A. 1095b). The ban also applies while stopped in traffic, at lights or in other short delays. Hands-free use is allowed, as are emergency calls, built-in or securely mounted GPS, and use while safely parked off the road.
laws.penalty_signal: First offence US$100 to US$200 and 2 licence points; a later offence within 2 years US$250 to US$500 (about A$142 to A$284, and A$355 to A$710, at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040). Higher in work zones and school zones: US$200 to US$400 first, US$500 to US$1,000 later, with 4 or 5 points.

laws.rule: Adults 21 and over may possess two ounces or less of cannabis or 10 grams or less of hashish. A person must not consume cannabis in a public place, as defined in 7 V.S.A. 831. Consuming cannabis while operating a motor vehicle remains an offence (18 V.S.A. 4230a). Cannabis stays illegal under US federal law, including on federal land.
laws.penalty_signal: civil penalty up to $100 first offence, $200 second, $500 third or later

items.text: Adults 21 and over may possess up to 2 ounces (about 57 g) of cannabis or 10 g of hashish without state penalty, raised from 1 ounce and 5 g from 1 July 2026 by Act 176 (Senate Bill 278, signed 18 June 2026). Home growing of up to 2 mature or 4 immature plants is allowed, and what is grown at home doesn't count toward the limit (18 V.S.A. 4230a).

No one may consume cannabis in a public place. The civil penalty is up to US$100 for a first offence, US$200 for a second and US$500 for a third or later (about A$142, A$284 and A$710 at RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = USD 0.7040).
